GASTROINTESTINAL__Oesophagus:
Overview — The Oesophagus & the General Gut-Tube Plan

The oesophagus is a muscular tube that conducts the bolus from pharynx to stomach by peristalsis. As the first GI note it is the place to learn the four-layer plan shared by the whole gut tube.

🔬 Image slot — oesophagus wall in cross-section — the four concentric layers
Layer (in→out)Contents
MucosaEpithelium + lamina propria + muscularis mucosae
SubmucosaDense CT, vessels, glands + submucosal (Meissner) plexus
Muscularis externaInner circular + outer longitudinal muscle + myenteric (Auerbach) plexus between them
Adventitia / serosaOuter CT (adventitia) or mesothelium-covered (serosa)
Memorise this mucosa → submucosa → muscularis externa → adventitia/serosa plan once; every GI organ is a variation on it. Meissner plexus in the submucosa (secretion); Auerbach between the muscle layers (motility).
How to Recognise the Oesophagus ⭐
🔬 Image slot — oesophagus — non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium over submucosal mucous glands
  • Non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium — built for abrasion resistance against the passing bolus (the defining clue).
  • Submucosal mucous glands (“oesophageal glands proper”) lubricate the lumen — one of the few sites with true submucosal glands (the other classic is the duodenum: Brunner glands).
  • Usually an adventitia (retroperitoneal/thoracic), not a serosa — except the short intra-abdominal part.
Stratified squamous + submucosal glands + adventitia → oesophagus. Absence of a serosa contributes to the poor containment of oesophageal perforations & tumour spread.
Muscularis Externa — a Skeletal-to-Smooth Transition
1
Upper thirdSkeletal muscle (voluntary start of swallowing)
2
Middle thirdMixed skeletal & smooth
3
Lower thirdSmooth muscle (involuntary peristalsis)
Swallowing starts voluntarily (skeletal, upper) and finishes as an involuntary peristaltic wave (smooth, lower), coordinated by the myenteric plexus & vagus.
The Gastro-Oesophageal Junction
🔬 Image slot — gastro-oesophageal junction — abrupt squamous-to-columnar Z-line
  • An abrupt transition (the “Z-line”) from oesophageal stratified squamous to gastric simple columnar epithelium.
  • Mucous cardiac glands guard each end of the oesophagus.
  • The lower oesophageal sphincter is mainly physiological (tone + diaphragmatic crura + angle of His) — not a thick anatomical ring.
Reflux across an incompetent LOS damages the squamous lining — the starting point for oesophagitis → Barrett’s → adenocarcinoma.
Stains
  • H&E — stratified squamous mucosa, submucosal glands, the muscularis transition & the Z-line.
  • Alcian blue / PAS — highlights goblet cells (intestinal metaplasia) in Barrett’s oesophagus.
Clinical / Pathological Correlate
GORD / reflux oesophagitis
Acid reflux → basal-cell hyperplasia, eosinophils/neutrophils in the squamous mucosa
Barrett’s oesophagus
Squamous → columnar intestinal metaplasia with goblet cells; premalignant → adenocarcinoma
Adenocarcinoma
Lower third, from Barrett’s; rising incidence in the West
Squamous cell carcinoma
Upper/mid third; risk: smoking, alcohol, hot drinks, Plummer-Vinson
Achalasia
Loss of myenteric (Auerbach) ganglion cells → failure of LOS relaxation; “bird-beak” on barium
Oesophageal varices
Portal hypertension dilates submucosal veins → life-threatening haematemesis
Two cancers, two ends: squamous cell carcinoma (upper/mid, smoking/alcohol) vs adenocarcinoma (lower, Barrett’s/reflux). Also know Mallory-Weiss (mucosal tear from vomiting) vs Boerhaave (full-thickness rupture).
⭐ Exam Pearls
Gut-tube plan: mucosa (epithelium+lamina propria+muscularis mucosae) → submucosa → muscularis externa → adventitia/serosa.
Meissner plexus = submucosa (secretion); Auerbach plexus = between muscle layers (motility).
Oesophagus = non-keratinised stratified squamous + submucosal mucous glands + usually adventitia (no serosa).
Muscularis externa: upper 1/3 skeletal, middle mixed, lower 1/3 smooth.
Z-line = abrupt squamous-to-columnar change at the GO junction; LOS is mostly physiological.
Barrett’s = squamous → columnar metaplasia with goblet cells → adenocarcinoma risk.
SCC = upper/mid (smoking/alcohol); adenocarcinoma = lower (Barrett’s).
Achalasia = loss of myenteric ganglion cells → bird-beak; varices = portal hypertension.
